doc.title: Derek Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

chapter: Studio work and the Basie connection
title: Reading at North Texas State and advice to students
summary: Talk of reading faded manuscripts and Smith lecturing seniors at North Texas State about the real world.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: They have a saying at some of the bigger music schools like North Texas State, they say you’ve got to be able to read fly crap.

The reason why I say that because you know a lot of jazz manuscripts are just scribbled or in pencil, and the stuff is faded and you’re reading it in a night club where there’s barely any light and there’s smoke all in your eyes, you know. So you’ve got to be able to read anything.

Yeah. I remember being down there. Well now I’m a kind of a -- I’m a veteran. I’m a seasoned veteran, you know, so now they hire me at North Texas State to come down and lecture the kids. Because there, the senior class, they’re all 22. They play wonderfully because they’ve got no experience in the outside world at all. So first of all, I say this wonderful music you’ve been playing, forget that. This is the real world when you get out there. And you’ve got to know some songs. And so I’m telling them a lot of songs that you should know. And don’t come in dressed the way you’re dressed because you’ll never get hired again. But that’s a good school. And the youngsters there are wonderful.
